L3@P0: 1 General description
L4@P0: The TJA1101B is a 100BASE-T1-compliant Ethernet PHY optimized for automotive use
L5@P0: cases such as gateways, IP camera links, radar modules, driver assistance systems and
L6@P0: back-bone networks. The device provides 100 Mbit/s transmit and receive capability over
L7@P0: a single unshielded twisted-pair cable, supporting a cable length of up to at least 15 m.
L8@P0: The TJA1101B has been designed for automotive robustness and ISO 26262, ASIL-A
L9@P0: compliance, while minimizing power consumption and system costs.
L10@P0: Being ASIL-A compliant, adequate safety features have been implemented to ensure that
L11@P0: ASIL requirements are met at system level. Additional documentation, including a safety
L12@P0: manual, is available on request.
L13@P0: The TJA1101B supports OPEN Alliance TC-10-compliant sleep and wake-up request
L14@P0: forwarding, with an always-on power domain connected directly to the battery supply
L15@P0: without the need for a dedicated voltage regulator.
L16@P0: 2 Features and benefits
L17@P0: 2.1 General
L18@P0: • 100BASE-T1 PHY
L19@P0: • MII- and RMII-compliant interfaces
L20@P0: • Compact 36-pin HVQFN package (6 × 6 mm) for PCB space-constrained applications
L21@P0: • ISO 26262, ASIL-A compliant
L22@P0: 2.2 Optimized for automotive use cases
L23@P0: • Transmitter optimized for capacitive coupling to unshielded twisted-pair cable
L24@P0: • Adaptive receive equalizer optimized for automotive cable length of up to at least 15 m
L25@P0: • Enhanced integrated PAM-3 pulse shaping for low RF emissions
L26@P0: • EMC-optimized output driver strength for MII and RMII
L27@P0: • MDI pins meet class IV conducted emission limit as per OPEN Alliance EMC
L28@P0: Specification 2.0
L29@P0: • MDI pins protected against ESD to ±6 kV HBM and ±8 kV IEC61000-4-2
L30@P0: • MDI pins protected against transients in automotive environment
L31@P0: • MDI pins do not need external filtering or ESD protection
L32@P0: • Automotive-grade temperature range from -40 °C to +125 °C
L33@P0: • Automotive product qualification in accordance with AEC-Q100
L34@P0: • Host-configurable MDI polarity
L35@P0-1: • Automated polarity detection and correctionNXP Semiconductors TJA1101B
L36@P1: 100BASE-T1 PHY for automotive Ethernet
L37@P1: 2.3 Low-power mode
L38@P1: • OPEN Alliance TC-10-compliant sleep and wake-up forwarding
L39@P1: – Robust remote wake-up detection via bus lines
L40@P1: – Wake-up forwarding at PHY level (supporting global system wake-up)
L41@P1: • Inhibit output for voltage regulator control
L42@P1: • Dedicated PHY enable/disable input pin to minimize power consumption
L43@P1: • Local wake-up pin
L44@P1: • Wake-up via SMI-access
L45@P1: 2.4 Diagnosis
L46@P1: • Signal Quality Indicator for real-time monitoring of link stability and transmitted data
L47@P1: quality
L48@P1: • Diagnosis of cable errors (shorts and opens)
L49@P1: • Gap-free supply undervoltage detection with fail-silent behavior
L50@P1: • Internal, external and remote loopback modes
L51@P1: 2.5 Miscellaneous
L52@P1: • Reverse MII mode for back-to-back connection of two PHYs
L53@P1: • On-chip regulators to provide 3.3 V single-supply operation
L54@P1: • Supports optional 1.8 V external supply for digital core
L55@P1: • On-chip termination resistors for the differential cable pair
L56@P1: • Jumbo frame support up to 16 kB

L68@P2: 4 Block diagram
L69@P2: A block diagram of the TJA1101B is shown in Figure 1. The 100BASE-T1 section
L70@P2: contains the functional blocks specified in the 100BASE-T1 standard that make up the
L71@P2: Physical Coding Sublayer (PCS) and the Physical Medium Attachment (PMA) layer for
L72@P2: both the transmit and receive signal paths. The MII/RMII interface (including the Serial
L73@P2: Management Interface (SMI)) conforms to IEEE 802.3 clause 22.
L74@P2: Additional blocks are defined for mode control, register configuration, interrupt control,
L75@P2: system configuration, reset control, local wake-up, remote wake-up, undervoltage
L76@P2: detection and configuration control. A number of power-supply-related functional blocks
L77@P2: are defined: an internal 1.8 V regulator for the digital core, a Very Low Power (VLP)
L78@P2: supply for Sleep mode, the reset circuit, supply monitoring and inhibit control.
L79@P2: The clock signals needed for the operation of the PHY are generated in the PLL block,
L80@P2: derived from an external crystal or an oscillator input signal.
L81@P2: Pin strapping allows a number of default PHY settings (e.g. Master or Slave
L82@P2: configuration) to be hardware-configured at power-up.
